correctness.rationale: Exact verification of piecewise Feres branch weights against the enumerated complete graph yields reversible sine weights and two parallel parity paths. Both path resistances are 4 alpha^-2 log n + O(alpha^-2); parity-local weighted Poincare is O(alpha^-2). Variational upper/lower Rayleigh inequalities then yield 1-lambda2 ~ 2 alpha^2/log n with correct 2 pi^2 n^-2 constant. Finite branch-matrix and edge checks, stationarity, detailed balance and symmetric eigenvalues pass in the standalone checker.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2007 original Feres billiard chapter, 2020 circular embedding and 2022 constant-curvature extension identify the maps, finite rational dihedral orbits, invariant sine law and qualitative mixing but do not state this logarithmic n-dependent finite-class spectral gap or constant. The other inspected random-billiard spectral results use different curved microstructures/Legendre limits, and the indexed mathematical-record comparisons yielded no equivalent or strictly stronger theorem. Bibliographic priority remains a nonzero risk.
residual_risks: Additional 2007–2026 billiard/finite weighted-cycle work could independently contain equivalent logarithmic gap behavior without using Feres model keywords.
The 2010 curved-cell paper was compared in accessible abstract/introduction only, not comprehensively all internal lemmas; geometry differs, but priority remains a residual risk.
Finite numerical eigenvalues are corroborative and not a substitute for analytical asymptotics.

value.rationale: The 2020 random circular billiard has natural finite invariant angle classes for rational triangular scattering. The exact class spectral gap measures relaxation that the previously qualitative mixing/nonmixing dichotomy does not quantify. An unanticipated logarithmic correction and sharp 2 pi^2 coefficient explain an arithmetic parity bottleneck from grazing angles, providing a structural benchmark rather than a routine isolated matrix evaluation.
